clues: An exceptional diversity of fish makes this protected waterscape important for the study of evolution.
Many of its fish species are endemic, giving isolation and diversification a central role in its significance.
Rocky shores, sandy bays, wooded hills and lagoons form a varied lake-edge landscape.
The park lies at the southern end of a deep, clear lake in the East African Rift system.
Find the World Heritage protected area on the southern shore of the great lake that shares its name with Malawi.
targetLabel: Lake Malawi National Park — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: The answer is the designated national park at the lake’s southern end rather than the whole lake. Its fish diversity makes ecological and evolutionary questions geographically meaningful. The source’s park reference point is used; the wider lake and rift system extend far beyond it.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
